hints.title: Translate the two crossings
hints.body: Use the discriminant condition for two distinct real roots. Identify all three coefficients of this quadratic.
hints.recap: Two distinct roots require a strictly positive discriminant.
hints.pitfall: The leading coefficient is p, and the constant term is also p.

recall.reminder: Two distinct roots require a strictly positive discriminant.

hints.title: Keep both possible signs
hints.body: Factor your difference of squares and solve the resulting product inequality, using p>0.
hints.recap: A product is positive when both nonzero factors have the same sign.
hints.pitfall: Do not discard a negative possibility when undoing a square.
hints.pause: Draw the boundary lines and decide which side of each is allowed.

recall.reminder: A product is positive when both nonzero factors have the same sign.

hints.title: Check the shaded regions
hints.body: Use a point between your lines and a point on each outside region to test the diagrams.
hints.recap: A test point can decide which side of a line satisfies an inequality.
hints.pitfall: Check the line slopes and whether their boundaries are included.
hints.pause: Choose the diagram matching your complete inequalities.

recall.reminder: A test point can decide which side of a line satisfies an inequality.

solution:
The discriminant is q2−4p2. Two distinct real roots require q2−4p2>0.

Because p>0, this is equivalent to q>2p or q<−2p. The boundary lines are excluded, since there the root is repeated.

The region therefore consists of the two wedges above q=2p and below q=−2p in the p>0 half-plane. This is graph F.
knowledgePattern: Map a discriminant inequality onto a two-sided parameter region
